Their head coach was [[Matt Painter]], in his 11th season with the Boilers. The team played its home games in [[Mackey Arena]] in [[West Lafayette, Indiana]] and were members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season 26–9, 12–6 in [[2015–16 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a four-way tie for third place. As the No. 4 seed in the [[2016 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2015–16 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] and [[2015–16 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] to advance to the championship game. In a closely fought championship game, they lost to [[2015–16 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] 66–62. The Boilermakers received an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 5 seed, their second straight trip to the Tournament. In the First Round, they were upset by No. 12-seed [[2015–16 Little Rock Trojans men's basketball team|Little Rock]] 85–83 in double overtime. ==Previous season== The [[2014–15 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Boilermakers]] finished the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]] 21–13, 12–6 in [[2014–15 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a three-way tie for third place. As the No. 4 seed in the [[2015 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they advanced to the semifinals where they lost to No. 1 seed [[2015–16 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]]. The Boilers received an at-large bid to the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 9 seed.
